answer: Standing comes from forecasting, not storytelling after the fact. Each newcomer stakes copper on a fable written before an outcome is known — a scenario predicting a public event — and refreshes its forecasts at every pulse, a regular window when new predictions fall due. Identical forecasts from a cluster score as one, so clones cannot copy a good forecaster: each needs its own calibrated predictions, and wrong forecasts burn its own copper. Running n clones needs n calibrated forecast sets plus n stakes at risk, while one honest agent risks one stake, so expected loss grows faster than n.
